tokyo_chinya.price_note: ⚠ THE PRICES BELOW ARE MAIL-ORDER, NOT RESTAURANT PRICES, AND THAT DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE CAVEAT. The page at chinya.co.jp/menu/ turns out to be the shop’s ONLINE SHOP — raw sukiyaki meat sets, miso-cured meat and tsukudani sold by weight for delivery — rather than the dining-room board. No in-restaurant dish, course or price is published anywhere on the site that was read. The items are recorded because they are real, priced and first-party, and because their composition is informative; they are not what you would be served at a table. Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ WHAT THE PRODUCT NAMES ESTABLISH FOR A COELIAC, AND IT IS THE ONE THING THAT MATTERS AT ANY SUKIYAKI HOUSE: every meat set is sold 割下付き — WITH WARISHITA, the sukiyaki cooking liquid, which is soy sauce, mirin and sugar. Sukiyaki is not meat with a sauce on the side; the warishita is the medium the beef is cooked in, so there is no version of the dish without it unless the kitchen will do a salt-and-oil 関西風 preparation, which nothing here mentions. Sukiyaki is also conventionally dipped in raw EGG. ⚠ AND THE SET PRODUCTS NAME THEIR OWN VEGETABLES: ザク (the vegetable mix), 白滝 (shirataki, konjac noodles — plant and wheat-free, unlike every other noodle in this dataset) and 焼き豆腐 (grilled tofu). Those three are the parts of a sukiyaki a plant-eater could in principle eat, and they arrive in a pan of soy-based beef stock.

The batter is wheat flour, and the shop’s stated house style makes it worse rather than better: it says the traditional way to eat here is to steep the piece in 秘伝の天つゆ with grated daikon, and tenzuyu is dashi plus soy plus mirin — wheat AND fish in one dip. It now resolves to an online-casino affiliate site (オンカジ入金不要ボーナス…) and must not be cited or followed. The live brand pages are under the operator, C-United, at c-united.co.jp/coffeekan/. ⚠ SECOND, EVERY PRICE BELOW IS A RANGE AND THAT IS HOW THE CHAIN PUBLISHES IT: each product page prints a low and a high figure (e.g. ¥590~¥850) because store tiers differ, with a 価格が違う店舗リスト PDF naming the dearer shops — that PDF is a graphical scan whose store names do not extract as text, so it could NOT be checked whether 渋谷店 is a standard or premium-tier store. tokyo_tainan_tami_shinjuku_hon.price_note: The complete 80-line grand menu, lunch sets, recommendations and drink list for the 新宿本店 specifically — the shop keeps SEPARATE menu pages for 新宿店 (shinjuku01) and 新宿職安通り店 (shinjuku02), and only the 新宿店 page is used here. Prices as printed; the lunch sets are marked 税込 and the rest are printed without a tax marker. The site is served in Shift_JIS and has to be transcoded before it reads. 台南担仔麺 is a Taiwanese yatai-style house in Kabukicho whose 280 yen 担仔麺 is a deliberately small signature bowl, not a main. ⚠ THE 280 YEN SIGNATURE IS WHEAT: 担仔麺 is a wheat noodle in a minced-pork sauce, and its stablemate 担米粉 at the same price is RICE VERMICELLI — that swap is the single most useful line on this card for a coeliac, and it is the shop’s own pairing, not an inference. The same logic runs down the noodle section: 米粉 (beehoon) dishes are rice, 麺 dishes are wheat, and the menu writes 炒米粉（麺）and 海鮮米粉（麺）to show you may have either — so those two must be ordered explicitly as 米粉. ⚠ EVERYTHING ELSE IS SOY. Taiwanese home cooking is built on 醬油 and 醬油膏, so the braises (魯味, 香豚足, 舌, 富貴耳), the 肉燥 minced-pork sauce over 油飯 and 豆菜, the 割包 and the stir-fries are all wheat by default; 酸辣湯 is additionally starch-thickened and vinegared. ⚠ AND TWO ITEMS ARE NOT WHAT THEY LOOK LIKE: 菜頭粿 (daikon cake) is daikon and RICE flour and so is one of the few genuinely non-wheat fried items, while 蚵仔煎 (oyster omelette) looks like okonomiyaki but is bound with SWEET POTATO STARCH, not wheat — both still ask, because the sauces poured over them are soy-based and no allergen statement is published. The menu prints several Chinese characters as ? where the site’s Shift_JIS encoding fails; those are reproduced as printed rather than guessed.

tokyo_vejiro_shibuya_sohonten_.price_note: NO PRICES ARE PUBLISHED ANYWHERE FIRST-PARTY, so every line below is unpriced — and the reason is that the only page the operator maintains for ベジ郎 is a FRANCHISE RECRUITMENT page, not a shop page. The 21 figures on it are joining fees and fit-out costs, not dish prices; they are deliberately NOT recorded here. What the page does give, and gives precisely, is the brand’s whole menu structure in FoodSupply’s own words, which is worth having: 野菜炒め and 肉野菜炒め each in 醤油 / ぽん酢 / 味噌; meat upgrades 中盛 100g, 大盛 150g, 特盛 200g; 定食 = the stir-fry plus rice and soup; vegetable quantity 少なめ 300g, 普通 400g, マシ 500g, マシマシ 600g; back fat 中油 20g, 大油 40g, 鬼油 80g, or なし; toppings coriander or butter; drinks Kirin Ichiban Shibori draught, Hon-shibori lemon, black oolong tea. It also names 3 regional extras (あんかけ揚げ餃子, ニラチャーハン, 玉子チャーハン) as EXAMPLES of what a franchisee might develop — those are NOT recorded as sold at the 渋谷総本店. FoodSupply is a vegetable wholesaler supplying about 5,000 restaurants, and the concept is one shop eating 200 kg of vegetables a day against a 20 kg industry average; the stir-fry is 400 g of vegetables with back fat. ⚠ ALL THREE SAUCES FAIL A COELIAC AND ONE OF THEM LOOKS LIKE IT SHOULD NOT: 醤油 is wheat outright, 味噌 is usually blended with soy sauce or mirin in a stir-fry seasoning, and ぽん酢 — the one people reach for as the light option — IS SOY SAUCE with citrus in it. There is no plain-salt option on the published matrix. No allergen information is published at all.

tokyo_banh_xeo_saigon_tokyo_do.price_note: EMPTY BECAUSE THE CHAIN PUBLISHES NO MENU FOR THIS BRANCH, and the near-miss is worth recording so nobody repeats it. vietnam-banhxeo.com (operator P4 inc.) is a single-page brand site: it explains what bánh xèo is and lists all four Tokyo shops — 有楽町, 新宿, 東京ドームシティ and 虎ノ門 — with address, phone and hours, but has no menu page at all (/menu/ returns 404). Only the 新宿 branch has its own subdomain, shinjuku.vietnam-banhxeo.com, and even that has no menu section — just こだわり, 物語, 新着情報, アクセス and a Toreta booking link, with the current offers announced in news posts. The 東京ドームシティ店 (文京区後楽1-3-61 黄色いビル 2F, Food Stadium Tokyo, 11:00-23:00) has only Instagram and Facebook. Carrying the Shinjuku shop’s course or lunch offers across to the Dome City branch would break the no-cross-branch rule, so nothing is recorded. WHAT THE BRAND PAGE DOES ESTABLISH, and it matters for anyone reading this later: the shop’s own description says the bánh xèo batter is 米粉 (RICE FLOUR) coloured with turmeric, filled with bean sprouts, pork and prawn, wrapped in leaf vegetables and dipped in nước chấm — so the pancake itself is not wheat. The dip is the problem: nước chấm is fish sauce, which is not vegan and is only sometimes wheat-free. None of that is branch-specific enough to record as items.

tokyo_asakusa_rairaiken.price_note: NO MENU COULD BE READ, AND THE REASON IS THE PLATFORM RATHER THAN THE SHOP. The site for 浅草来々軒 is built on STUDIO (studio.site), a Nuxt single-page app that ships an empty HTML shell and paints the page from JavaScript. curl and WebFetch both return only the site title and a STUDIO banner. This tick went further than a fetch: STUDIO publishes each site's content as a snapshot JSON in Google Cloud Storage, and the app's own __NUXT_DATA__ payload names the exact path. That snapshot was retrieved and parsed — and its "components" key is an empty object, so the text simply is not in the published payload this egress can reach. Menu subpaths (/menu, /food, /drink) were probed as well and either 404 or return the same shell. This is a COMPLETE result for a text-only harvest: the shop may well display a full menu to a real browser, but nothing was found that could be quoted, and nothing has been guessed. A future pass with a headless browser that executes JavaScript is the way to finish this record; a re-fetch will not be. ⚠ FOR PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY, NOT AS A MENU CLAIM: the shop is recorded in this dataset as 中華料理, and a Chinese restaurant in Japan is a wheat-dominant kitchen — ramen, gyoza, and soy-sauce seasoning throughout. Nothing here should be read as a finding about a specific dish, because no dish was found.

tokyo_mafumi_coffee_shop_shint.price_note: HOST RESOLVES BUT REFUSES CONNECTIONS. 眞踏珈琲店's site is on a free XDOMAIN subdomain; the name coffeemafumi.html.xdomain.jp resolves cleanly to 157.112.147.44, but every connection attempt fails — curl returns exit 000 on http and https, on both / and /index.html, and WebFetch reports ECONNREFUSED on port 443. DNS is fine and the host is refusing the socket, which usually means the hosting account has lapsed while the DNS record survives. Worth one retry on a later tick in case it is transient, but a refused connection on a free-hosting subdomain more often means the site is gone. Nothing was read. The dataset's menu_url is Tabelog, unreachable from this egress. 眞踏珈琲店 is recorded as 喫茶店・コーヒー — a kissaten. ⚠ Standing kissaten note: the coffee itself is not the risk; the risk is that a Japanese kissaten counter almost always serves toast, sandwiches and hotcakes from the same small workspace, so cross-contamination is the question to ask rather than the drink.

tokyo_pho_hanoi_yatai_33_lumin.price_note: Address confirmed on the shop's own HotPepper page as 新宿区新宿3-38-1 ルミネエスト新宿 8F, which is the record's branch; the listing trades as ベトナム料理 フォーハノイ屋台33 rather than the longer name. Prices 税込. ⚠ THIS IS THE MOST GLUTEN-LEGIBLE KITCHEN IN THE BATCH AND ALSO THE MOST BOOBY-TRAPPED, because the good news and the bad news arrive on the same plate. The good news: フォー and ブン are RICE noodles, the 蒸し春巻き is a steamed 米粉 (rice-flour) crêpe, and the shop states twice that it fries in rice flour — 鶏なんこつのヌクマム揚げ is 「米粉で揚げた」 and so is the ベトナム風レモングラス米粉衣の鶏の唐揚げ, which is a rice-flour-battered fried chicken and a genuinely rare thing to find on a Tokyo menu. ⚠ THE BAD NEWS IS THE SET. Every 麺セット on this card ships with 生春巻き, 揚げパン, raw vegetables, coriander, lemon, chilli and a チェー — and the 揚げパン is a deep-fried WHEAT dough that the shop tells you to tear up and dunk in the soup, while the fresh spring roll comes with a peanut sauce. Order the noodle bowl and the wheat arrives beside it unasked. Ask for the set without the 揚げパン. ⚠ Every バインミー is a wheat baguette by definition. ⚠ VEGAN: the shop labels 野菜の生春巻き a 「ヴィーガン生春巻き」 and runs a ヴィーガンメニュー heading whose one entry is 厚揚げのせ まぜそば. Treat 厚揚げと野菜のフォー as vegetarian-leaning rather than vegan — the shop calls it ヘルシー because it has no meat, but Vietnamese pho stock and ヌクマム fish sauce are not vegan and the shop does not claim they are.

tokyo_hatonomori_suidobashi.price_note: No menu could be obtained for this shop from any source that still works, so this is an honest empty. ⚠ EVERY PUBLISHED ROUTE TO THIS RESTAURANT IS NOW BROKEN, AND THE PATTERN SUGGESTS IT HAS STOPPED TRADING. The record's URL https://gewb402.gorp.jp/ returns Gnavi's 404 page (「ご指定のページが見つかりません」). The matching Gnavi shop page r.gnavi.co.jp/jnst68u00000/ no longer serves shop content either — the menu URL renders only Gnavi's generic site chrome. The Lets Enjoy Tokyo listing enjoytokyo.jp/gourmet/spot/g_gewb402/ returns 404. Four independent listings taken down is not a platform glitch; that is what delisting looks like. ⚠ DO NOT LINK THE SHOP'S OLD DOMAIN. suidobashi.hatonomori.com still answers on plain HTTP, but it no longer serves the restaurant: it now returns a redirect interstitial that stamps a per-visit tracking id onto the URL (?tr_uuid=...&fp=-5) and bounces the visitor on through a script-computed target — the standard signature of a lapsed domain resold for traffic monetisation. Microsoft Defender on this machine quarantined the response as unwanted software on download. Whatever is on that host, it is not a menu, and it should not be put in front of a user. ⚠ THE ONLY LISTING STILL STANDING is Hitosara, which is a directory that keeps entries long after shops close and whose copy here is visibly stale (it still carries a COVID-era sanitising notice and has no user photos). What it records, for whatever it is worth: 東京都千代田区三崎町2-16-10, four minutes from JR Suidobashi south exit, 03-6261-6666, dinner only on weekdays and days before holidays, CLOSED SATURDAYS SUNDAYS AND PUBLIC HOLIDAYS, average spend ¥4,500. It lists no dishes and no prices. ⚠ IF IT IS TRADING, THE DIET ANSWER IS ALREADY CLEAR from what the concept is: a mutton yakiniku and jingisukan house whose selling point is unfrozen mutton shipped from Iida in Nagano and a secret-recipe dipping sauce reconstructed from an Iida restaurant. Jingisukan tare is a soy-sauce, fruit and mirin blend, so wheat, and the whole premise is grilled sheep. Nothing here is plausible for either diet. Telephone before travelling; do not rely on any of these links.

tokyo_menya_sarusuberi_hyakuji.price_note: ⚠ ONE PRICE, AND IT IS THE INTERESTING ONE. A Tokyo eating blog that visited on 2025-08-17 photographed the ticket machine but its write-up carries only a single figure: the 500円朝ラー, a five-hundred-yen morning ramen served on weekdays from 7:00 to 11:00. Hitosara was read and confirms the shop and its 11:00〜23:00 daytime hours but publishes no menu at all. Instagram is the shop’s only listed channel and serves a login wall to this egress; Tabelog has served HTTP 403 to this egress since 2026-09-02. The dish names and portion structure below are from the ticket machine and are solid; the prices for them are not published anywhere readable and are recorded as such rather than guessed. ⚠ WHERE IT IS, WHICH IS MOST OF THE APPEAL: B1F of the Keio Frente building at Shinjuku-sanchōme, connected by underground passage to both Shinjuku-sanchōme and Shinjuku stations — so it can be reached in a downpour or a heatwave without going outside. Trading since 2010. ⚠ THE PORTION RULE IS WORTH KNOWING AND IS NOT OBVIOUS: 並盛 200g, 大盛 300g AT THE SAME PRICE, 特盛 400g. A free 50% upgrade is unusual enough to be the single most useful practical fact about this shop. ⚠ DIET: the house line is 煮干し — DRIED SARDINE — which is a whole small fish boiled and dried, and it is the broth rather than a garnish, so both the signature tsukemen and the signature soba are fish dishes with no variant that is not. The 淡麗塩つけ麺 the blog ate is described as a clear brown broth with white spring onion and aonori seaweed, containing chicken and seared chopped chashu plus thin crunchy menma — chicken and pork on top of it. Every noodle here is wheat. There is nothing on the published board without an animal in it.

items.en: The morning ramen — a bowl for five hundred yen, weekday mornings only, from seven until eleven. The shop’s value proposition and the reason people know it
items.note: どの銘柄の丼が朝ラーになるかは未掲載。Which bowl the morning price applies to is not published. Whatever it is, it is a wheat noodle in a soy or salt tare at a shop whose stock is dried sardine — fish — so nothing about the hour changes the ingredients.

tokyo_kuroge_wagyu_ichinoya_as.price_note: ⭐ THE SHOP IS CALLED 黒毛和牛 壱乃屋 AND TWO OF ITS FIVE BOWLS ARE NOT 黒毛和牛. Read the bracketed sourcing on each line: the 6,600円 chateaubriand, the 5,500円 fillet and the 3,500円 bowl all say 黒毛和牛使用 — Japanese Black wagyu. The 2,500円 and 2,200円 bowls say 国産牛, which means cattle raised in Japan and is a completely different and much weaker claim: any breed, any dairy cross, no wagyu grading implied. Both terms are legitimate and the shop is not hiding anything — it prints the distinction on every line — but the shop NAME advertises the better one, and a visitor ordering the cheapest bowl under that sign is not eating what the sign says. That is the single most useful thing on this menu and it is invisible in the English rendering, which drops the bracket contents to "Japanese Beef". ⚠ DIETARY PICTURE, AND IT IS SHORT: five beef bowls, no non-meat option of any kind, so this is simply not a shop a vegetarian can use. For gluten the answer is ask-but-assume-no: the rice under the beef is naturally gluten-free, but レアステーキ重 and 焼肉丼 are both finished with a tare, and Japanese steak and yakiniku sauces are soy-based, which is wheat. Nobody publishes an allergen sheet. ⚠ FOUR OF THE FIVE BOWLS ARE SERVED RARE — レアステーキ重 means the beef is deliberately undercooked, which is a normal and safe preparation in Japan for whole-muscle beef but is worth knowing if you are pregnant, immunocompromised, or simply not expecting it. ⭐ ONE TRANSLATION TO DISTRUST: Tabelog's English calls the 3,500円 cut "Brisket". The Chinese listing prints 肋條（カルビ） and the Korean prints 갈비 — カルビ is SHORT RIB, not brisket. Different cut, different fat content, different thing. ON THE LISTING: no 更新日, prices undated; recorded average spend 3,000–3,999円, which is consistent with the middle of this list. Open 11:00–21:00, closed Thursdays, 16 seats, 浅草1-34-6 大阪屋ビル 1F. 重 in these names is the lacquered box the rice comes in, not a size.

BEEF, rare, soy tare assumed.
